10	
11	- Story 3.1: Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell
12	- Story 3.2: Audio Entry Capture & On-Device Transcription
13	- Story 3.3: Photo Entry Capture & Backend OCR
14	- Story 3.4: Cancel-Safe Capture Across All Tabs
15	
16	## Requirements & Constraints
17	
18	- All three capture modalities (text, audio, photo) must produce the same persisted Entry shape; `source` is `manual`/`audio`/`photo` respectively, and each `POST /entries` call must carry the correct one.
19	- Audio and photo Entries are only "complete" once processed: audio via on-device transcription, photo via backend OCR. The transcribed/recognized text is editable before the user taps Salvar; the Entry is only created on explicit save, not automatically after processing finishes.
20	- Audio transcription runs 100% on-device via `whisper_ggml`; no call in this pipeline may ever contain audio bytes. The audio pipeline has exactly four states in sequence: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry; the recorded media is never discarded on a transcription failure.
21	- Photo OCR calls the backend before the Entry is created, mirroring the same four-state shape: capture → processing OCR → recognized → error. `OCR_NO_TEXT` is a distinct, non-retryable outcome with two recovery paths: "Tentar novamente" (retry OCR on the same photo) and "Salvar só a foto" (save with no extracted text) — never a single generic failure message. An oversized photo returns non-retryable `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413); show a size-specific message with no retry button.
22	- Cancel-safety (FR-11) is absolute: interrupting a capture before Salvar — closing the modal, switching Insertion Modal tabs, backing out mid-photo, stopping a recording early — must never fire `POST /entries`. Opening the modal always resets all three tabs to idle/empty; switching tabs mid-capture cancels the in-flight capture outright (resolved ambiguity — the prototype itself left this undefined).
23	- Offline: the "+" entry point is disabled with the same offline-banner treatment as chat send. Capture requires a live `POST /entries` round trip (PII check + embedding), so there is no local-only queued write — a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `NetworkOffline`, never queued.
24	- Every screen-reader-relevant state transition needs an announced label ("Gravando," "Transcrevendo," "Erro ao transcrever, toque para tentar novamente," etc.) — color/animation alone never carries state.
25	
26	## Technical Decisions
27	
28	- Two feature modules split the work: `features/entries/` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create` + `read` only — no update/delete ever), and the entries `hive_ce` box. `features/capture/` owns the Insertion Modal UI, the on-device Whisper STT flow, and the OCR call, and holds no Entry data itself — it only consumes the abstract port from `entries/domain` (never imports `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`). This port is exactly what RF10 (Epic 6, save chat message as entry) and RF06/RF07 (Search, Timeline) will extend/reuse later — get its shape right here, not provisionally.
29	- `create` on the port is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`, though that specific guard only matters starting with RF10; this epic just needs to not violate the port's shape.
30	- Backend calls for this epic: `POST /entries` → function `entries-create`; `POST /media/ocr` → function `media-ocr` (the photo itself is not persisted server-side, only the extracted text comes back). Both calls follow the standard header rules (`apikey` always, `Authorization: Bearer <user token>`, since neither operation is one of the three `security: []` exceptions).
31	- Error handling: map the 13 backend error codes (plus the local-only `MalformedResponse`) to the one sealed `Failure` hierarchy already defined in `core/failure/`. For this epic specifically: `OcrNoText` and `PayloadTooLarge` are both non-retryable and need their own distinct UI treatment, not a generic error state. The retry interceptor fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes — OCR/payload failures are never auto-retried.
32	- The capture feature defines its own sealed state class for its multi-step audio/OCR state machines — it is explicitly excluded from using the shared generic `Resource<T>` type (`Resource<T>` is reserved for RF06/RF09's simpler single-fetch screens).
33	- The Insertion Modal's three tabs are internal states of one bottom sheet, never nested sheets; its entrance animation is the shared `sheetUp` (0.2s) choreography, with no other motion invented.
34	
35	## UX & Interaction Patterns
36	
37	- Insertion Modal: three equal-width tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto); only the active tab gets a filled `colorPrimary` background. A close ("x") control is always present. The modal opens on Texto by default.
38	- Audio tab: an animated multi-bar waveform with a monospace running timer while recording; on stop, the waveform freezes at 35% opacity with a "Transcrevendo..." label while processing (no spinner needed beyond that). Once transcribed, text is editable and "Salvar" enables; the original audio duration shows in monospace.
39	- Photo tab: thumbnail + spinner + "Reconhecendo texto..." while OCR runs. Once recognized, text is editable before Salvar.
40	- Dynamic Type and tap-target rules (≥44pt, no truncation at largest accessibility text size) apply to all controls built here, same as everywhere else in the app.
41	- Reduce Motion: this epic has no cursor-blink (that's Chat), but still must honor the `sheetUp`/`scrimIn`-only animation rule and skip it when Reduce Motion is on.
42	
43	## Cross-Story Dependencies
44	
45	- Story 3.1 is the first consumer of `features/entries/` and must stand up the `Entry` entity, `EntriesRepository` port (`create`), and the entries Hive box — Stories 3.2 and 3.3 build on top of this rather than creating their own local Entry model.
46	- Story 3.4 (cancel-safety) is a cross-cutting rule that applies to the tab/state machines built in 3.1–3.3; it's written as its own story but has no independent UI surface — it hardens behavior already present in the other three.
47	- This epic depends on Epic 2 (Biometric Vault): the Insertion Modal is only reachable once the vault is unlocked.
48	- Everything this epic builds in `features/entries/` is a hard dependency for Epic 4 (Timeline), Epic 5 (Search), and Epic 6's RF10 (save-to-journal) — those epics extend this port rather than replacing it.

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users capture a journal Entry through one shared Insertion Modal in three ways — typed text, recorded audio, or a photo — and every modality ends up as the same persisted `Entry` shape. Audio is transcribed entirely on-device; a photo's text is recognized server-side via OCR before the Entry exists. Text and audio/photo stay merged into one epic because an un-transcribed audio Entry or un-OCR'd photo Entry is not a usable product outcome on its own — "capture" and "process" are one milestone here, not two. The epic also guarantees interrupting any capture (switching tabs, backing out, stopping early) never leaves a stray partial or empty Entry behind. This is the first epic to introduce `features/entries/`, which every later epic that creates or reads an Entry (Timeline, Search, Chat save-to-journal) will consume through its port — so decisions made here about that port's shape are load-bearing for the rest of the app.

## Stories

- Story 3.1: Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell
- Story 3.2: Audio Entry Capture & On-Device Transcription
- Story 3.3: Photo Entry Capture & Backend OCR
- Story 3.4: Cancel-Safe Capture Across All Tabs

## Requirements & Constraints

- All three capture modalities (text, audio, photo) must produce the same persisted Entry shape; `source` is `manual`/`audio`/`photo` respectively, and each `POST /entries` call must carry the correct one.
- Audio and photo Entries are only "complete" once processed: audio via on-device transcription, photo via backend OCR. The transcribed/recognized text is editable before the user taps Salvar; the Entry is only created on explicit save, not automatically after processing finishes.
- Audio transcription runs 100% on-device via `whisper_ggml`; no call in this pipeline may ever contain audio bytes. The audio pipeline has exactly four states in sequence: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry; the recorded media is never discarded on a transcription failure.
- Photo OCR calls the backend before the Entry is created, mirroring the same four-state shape: capture → processing OCR → recognized → error. `OCR_NO_TEXT` is a distinct, non-retryable outcome with two recovery paths: "Tentar novamente" (retry OCR on the same photo) and "Salvar só a foto" (save with no extracted text) — never a single generic failure message. An oversized photo returns non-retryable `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413); show a size-specific message with no retry button.
- Cancel-safety (FR-11) is absolute: interrupting a capture before Salvar — closing the modal, switching Insertion Modal tabs, backing out mid-photo, stopping a recording early — must never fire `POST /entries`. Opening the modal always resets all three tabs to idle/empty; switching tabs mid-capture cancels the in-flight capture outright (resolved ambiguity — the prototype itself left this undefined).
- Offline: the "+" entry point is disabled with the same offline-banner treatment as chat send. Capture requires a live `POST /entries` round trip (PII check + embedding), so there is no local-only queued write — a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `NetworkOffline`, never queued.
- Every screen-reader-relevant state transition needs an announced label ("Gravando," "Transcrevendo," "Erro ao transcrever, toque para tentar novamente," etc.) — color/animation alone never carries state.

## Technical Decisions

- Two feature modules split the work: `features/entries/` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create` + `read` only — no update/delete ever), and the entries `hive_ce` box. `features/capture/` owns the Insertion Modal UI, the on-device Whisper STT flow, and the OCR call, and holds no Entry data itself — it only consumes the abstract port from `entries/domain` (never imports `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`). This port is exactly what RF10 (Epic 6, save chat message as entry) and RF06/RF07 (Search, Timeline) will extend/reuse later — get its shape right here, not provisionally.
- `create` on the port is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`, though that specific guard only matters starting with RF10; this epic just needs to not violate the port's shape.
- Backend calls for this epic: `POST /entries` → function `entries-create`; `POST /media/ocr` → function `media-ocr` (the photo itself is not persisted server-side, only the extracted text comes back). Both calls follow the standard header rules (`apikey` always, `Authorization: Bearer <user token>`, since neither operation is one of the three `security: []` exceptions).
- Error handling: map the 13 backend error codes (plus the local-only `MalformedResponse`) to the one sealed `Failure` hierarchy already defined in `core/failure/`. For this epic specifically: `OcrNoText` and `PayloadTooLarge` are both non-retryable and need their own distinct UI treatment, not a generic error state. The retry interceptor fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes — OCR/payload failures are never auto-retried.
- The capture feature defines its own sealed state class for its multi-step audio/OCR state machines — it is explicitly excluded from using the shared generic `Resource<T>` type (`Resource<T>` is reserved for RF06/RF09's simpler single-fetch screens).
- The Insertion Modal's three tabs are internal states of one bottom sheet, never nested sheets; its entrance animation is the shared `sheetUp` (0.2s) choreography, with no other motion invented.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Insertion Modal: three equal-width tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto); only the active tab gets a filled `colorPrimary` background. A close ("x") control is always present. The modal opens on Texto by default.
- Audio tab: an animated multi-bar waveform with a monospace running timer while recording; on stop, the waveform freezes at 35% opacity with a "Transcrevendo..." label while processing (no spinner needed beyond that). Once transcribed, text is editable and "Salvar" enables; the original audio duration shows in monospace.
- Photo tab: thumbnail + spinner + "Reconhecendo texto..." while OCR runs. Once recognized, text is editable before Salvar.
- Dynamic Type and tap-target rules (≥44pt, no truncation at largest accessibility text size) apply to all controls built here, same as everywhere else in the app.
- Reduce Motion: this epic has no cursor-blink (that's Chat), but still must honor the `sheetUp`/`scrimIn`-only animation rule and skip it when Reduce Motion is on.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 3.1 is the first consumer of `features/entries/` and must stand up the `Entry` entity, `EntriesRepository` port (`create`), and the entries Hive box — Stories 3.2 and 3.3 build on top of this rather than creating their own local Entry model.
- Story 3.4 (cancel-safety) is a cross-cutting rule that applies to the tab/state machines built in 3.1–3.3; it's written as its own story but has no independent UI surface — it hardens behavior already present in the other three.
- This epic depends on Epic 2 (Biometric Vault): the Insertion Modal is only reachable once the vault is unlocked.
- Everything this epic builds in `features/entries/` is a hard dependency for Epic 4 (Timeline), Epic 5 (Search), and Epic 6's RF10 (save-to-journal) — those epics extend this port rather than replacing it.

**Given** I type text and tap Salvar
**When** the save completes

**Given** `features/entries/` does not yet exist

### Story 3.2: Audio Entry Capture & On-Device Transcription

As a user,
I want to record audio in the Insertion Modal and have it transcribed on-device,

**Given** the audio file at any point in this pipeline
**When** any network call is inspected

### Story 3.3: Photo Entry Capture & Backend OCR

As a user,
I want to capture or select a photo in the Insertion Modal and have its text recognized,

**Given** the Foto tab

**Given** the photo exceeds the upload size limit
**When** `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413, non-retryable) is returned

input.prompt:
I'm planning Story 3.1 ("Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell") for a Flutter app called Cerne (Clean Architecture: data/domain/presentation layers per feature, `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart` Either, `freezed` Failure hierarchy, `hive_ce` for local storage, DI likely via `get_it`/`injectable`). The story needs to:
1. Introduce a new `lib/features/entries/` module: `Entry` entity, `EntriesRepository` port with a `create` method only, and a Hive box for entries.
2. Introduce (or extend) `lib/features/capture/` owning an "Insertion Modal" bottom sheet UI with three tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto) — this story only implements the Texto tab fully; Áudio/Foto are placeholder tabs (idle/empty, reset on open).
3. Wire the modal to a "+" entry point that should already exist as a placeholder from a previous story (Story 1.6: "Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders").
4. On Salvar, call `POST /entries` (function name `entries-create` per the project's `x-cerne-function` convention — base URL from `.env`'s `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`) with `source=manual`, close the modal.
5. Offline: the "+" entry point must be disabled with the same offline-banner treatment used elsewhere (e.g. chat send) — find if that pattern already exists anywhere in the codebase.
6. Map backend error codes to the existing sealed `Failure` hierarchy.

I need a DISTILLED report (not full file dumps) covering, with exact file paths and line numbers where relevant:
- Where is the "+" entry point placeholder from Story 1.6? What file, what widget/route, what's currently there (e.g. is it a no-op button, a TODO, a named route)?
- What does an existing feature module (e.g. `features/account`, `features/vault`, or whichever exists from epics 1-2) look like structurally — list its data/domain/presentation file tree as a pattern to mirror, and name one concrete repository implementation file as a model for `EntriesRepository`.
- Where is the sealed `Failure` hierarchy defined (`core/failure/`)? What does it look like (variant names), and is there an existing error-code-to-Failure mapper I should follow as a pattern?
- Where/how is the HTTP client configured (base URL from `.env`, `apikey` header, `Authorization: Bearer` header injection)? Is there a shared API client class already, and does it already handle the `x-cerne-function` URL construction convention?
- Where is `hive_ce` initialized/registered (box registration, adapters, DI wiring)? Show one existing box registration as a pattern.
- Where is DI configured (get_it/injectable or otherwise) — show how an existing feature registers its repository/datasource/bloc.
- Is there any existing "offline banner" or connectivity-check widget/service already built (used for chat send per the product spec) — if yes, where; if no, say clearly it doesn't exist yet.
- What does `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` currently expose that's relevant to a bottom-sheet modal, tab bar, and a "sheetUp" 0.2s entrance animation — are these tokens already present or need to be added?
- Any existing use-case/interactor pattern (e.g. in account or vault features) for calling a repository from a bloc/cubit, to mirror for "SaveTextEntry" or similar.
- Any existing `freezed`/`json_serializable` DTO pattern for request/response bodies posted to the backend, to mirror for the entries-create request/response.

Keep the report tight — this is going into a spec's "Code Map" section (annotated paths + line anchors + reuse pointers), not a narrative. Report back under 600 words, with exact `path:line` references everywhere possible.

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

1	import 'package:freezed_annotation/freezed_annotation.dart';
2	
3	part 'failure.freezed.dart';
4	
5	/// AD-3 — the one closed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes: the 13
6	/// codes from `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` plus the local-only
7	/// `malformedResponse` (client-side parse failure, never sent by the
8	/// backend). Never redefined or subset per feature; every repository method
9	/// returns `Either<Failure, T>` built from this type (RNF09).
10	///
11	/// `retryable` is derived here, once, from the 6 server `retryable:true`
12	/// codes (AD-4) — no other file re-decides which codes retry.
13	@freezed
14	sealed class Failure with _$Failure {
15	  const factory Failure.authExpired({required String message}) = AuthExpired;
16	  const factory Failure.authInvalid({required String message}) = AuthInvalid;
17	  const factory Failure.networkTimeout({required String message}) =
18	      NetworkTimeout;
19	  const factory Failure.networkOffline({required String message}) =
20	      NetworkOffline;
21	  const factory Failure.validation({required String message}) = Validation;
22	  const factory Failure.piiCheckFailed({required String message}) =
23	      PiiCheckFailed;
24	  const factory Failure.embeddingFailed({required String message}) =
25	      EmbeddingFailed;
26	  const factory Failure.aiGenerationTimeout({required String message}) =
27	      AiGenerationTimeout;
28	  const factory Failure.notFound({required String message}) = NotFound;
29	  const factory Failure.rateLimited({required String message}) = RateLimited;
30	  const factory Failure.exportEmptyPeriod({required String message}) =
31	      ExportEmptyPeriod;
32	  const factory Failure.payloadTooLarge({required String message}) =
33	      PayloadTooLarge;
34	  const factory Failure.ocrNoText({required String message}) = OcrNoText;
35	
36	  /// Local-only — the client's own parse-failure detection. `retryable` is
37	  /// hardcoded `false` for this subtype (AD-3).
38	  const factory Failure.malformedResponse({required String message}) =
39	      MalformedResponse;
40	
41	  const Failure._();
42	
43	  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes (AD-4). Every other code —
44	  /// including the local `malformedResponse` — is `false`.
45	  bool get retryable => switch (this) {
46	        NetworkTimeout() => true,
47	        NetworkOffline() => true,
48	        PiiCheckFailed() => true,
49	        EmbeddingFailed() => true,
50	        AiGenerationTimeout() => true,
51	        RateLimited() => true,
52	        AuthExpired() ||
53	        AuthInvalid() ||
54	        Validation() ||
55	        NotFound() ||
56	        ExportEmptyPeriod() ||
57	        PayloadTooLarge() ||
58	        OcrNoText() ||
59	        MalformedResponse() =>
60	          false,
61	      };
62	
63	  /// Maps a backend error `code` (`error-taxonomy.md`) to its `Failure`
64	  /// subtype. An unrecognized code (should never happen — the taxonomy is
65	  /// closed) falls back to [Failure.malformedResponse] rather than throwing,
66	  /// so no repository ever lets an unmapped error escape (RNF09).
67	  factory Failure.fromCode(String code, String message) => switch (code) {
68	        'AUTH_EXPIRED' => Failure.authExpired(message: message),
69	        'AUTH_INVALID' => Failure.authInvalid(message: message),
70	        'NETWORK_TIMEOUT' => Failure.networkTimeout(message: message),
71	        'NETWORK_OFFLINE' => Failure.networkOffline(message: message),
72	        'VALIDATION_ERROR' => Failure.validation(message: message),
73	        'PII_CHECK_FAILED' => Failure.piiCheckFailed(message: message),
74	        'EMBEDDING_FAILED' => Failure.embeddingFailed(message: message),
75	        'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT' =>
76	          Failure.aiGenerationTimeout(message: message),
77	        'NOT_FOUND' => Failure.notFound(message: message),
78	        'RATE_LIMITED' => Failure.rateLimited(message: message),
79	        'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD' => Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: message),
80	        'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE' => Failure.payloadTooLarge(message: message),
81	        'OCR_NO_TEXT' => Failure.ocrNoText(message: message),
82	        _ => Failure.malformedResponse(message: message),
83	      };
84	}

1	import '../../core/di/injection_container.dart';
2	import 'data/datasources/account_remote_data_source.dart';
3	import 'data/repositories/account_settings_repository_impl.dart';
4	import 'domain/repositories/account_settings_repository.dart';

7	/// Registers the `account` feature into the project's single `get_it`
8	/// instance (`sl`) — mirrors `features/vault/vault_injection.dart`'s
9	/// pattern. Called from `setupCoreDependencies()` right after
10	/// `registerVaultFeature()` (Code Map).
11	void registerAccountFeature() {
12	  sl.registerLazySingleton<AccountRemoteDataSource>(
13	    () => AccountRemoteDataSource(sl()),
14	  );
15	
16	  // The epic's one new DI-singleton access point for the account's
17	  // `biometricEnabled` preference — registered as a singleton so every
18	  // consumer (`main.dart`'s boot fetch; `core/navigation/app_router.dart`'s
19	  // `/vault` builder; the Configurações screen's own cubit) shares the same
20	  // `biometricEnabledStream`, not a fresh instance each. `dispose:` wires
21	  // `AccountSettingsRepository.dispose()` into `get_it`'s own reset
22	  // lifecycle, so `resetCoreDependencies()` (`sl.reset()`) closes its
23	  // `StreamController` instead of leaking one on every test teardown.
24	  sl.registerLazySingleton<AccountSettingsRepository>(
25	    () => AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl(remoteDataSource: sl()),
26	    dispose: (repository) => repository.dispose(),
27	  );
28	
29	  // Review finding: `AccountSettingsCubit`'s constructor subscribes to
30	  // `biometricEnabledStream`; only its own `close()` cancels that
31	  // subscription, which nothing previously called — `dispose:` wires it
32	  // into `get_it`'s own reset lifecycle, same convention as every other
33	  // registration in this file.
34	  sl.registerLazySingleton<AccountSettingsCubit>(
35	    () => AccountSettingsCubit(sl()),
36	    dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close(),
37	  );
38	}

_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:7:scope: 'Cerne Flutter/iOS app — all 11 build units (F000, RF01..RF10, requirements.md sec.12 delivery order). Governs the cross-unit invariants: layer boundaries, cross-feature access, shared core contracts, offline/sync semantics, and the stack decisions the F000 forge session already locked.'
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:101:### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:103:- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:104:- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:105:- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Plain reads (`GET /entries`, `GET /chat/sessions`, `GET .../messages`) transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. **Semantic search is the one read exception:** `GET /entries/search` has no client-side vector index to fall back to, so with no connectivity it also resolves to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)`, same as a write — it is never served from cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:111:- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from three inputs: `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and the transient per-entry write state (AD-9) — which is itself one of three values: no pending write (→ `Synchronized`), a write in flight (→ `Synchronizing`), or the in-flight write's `Future` resolved to `Left(Failure)` (→ `Synchronization error`, held until the next write attempt reconciles it). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:140:- **Prevents:** a unit adding local filtering, joining, or sorting logic "for performance" or "for offline support," which would then disagree with the server's own filter semantics (AD-9's offline read rule assumes the cache's content is a verbatim copy, not a re-derived view).
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:141:- **Rule:** every query dimension (`source`, `dateFrom`/`dateTo`, semantic search, pagination cursor) is a server-side query parameter per `openapi.yaml`. A `hive_ce` box stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id (or by session id for messages); no feature ever filters, joins, sorts, or re-derives a different view from a cached collection — a cache miss or a dimension not covered by AD-9's offline-read rule surfaces `Failure.networkOffline`, it is never approximated locally.
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:233:| RF01 — multimodal capture | `features/capture/` → `features/entries/` (introduces it) | AD-1, AD-2, AD-6, AD-9, AD-15 |
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:236:| RF06 — semantic search/filter | `features/entries/` (extends with search) | AD-9 (search carve-out), AD-12, AD-15 |
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md:237:| RF04 — chat with memory (RAG) | `features/chat/` | AD-1, AD-2, AD-9, AD-12 (own stream, excluded) |
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/reviews/review-adversarial.md:16:**Scenario.** Delivery order is `F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → …`. RF01's own acceptance criteria ("Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`)") makes RF01 — not RF07 — the first build unit that must create entries, and it is built two full units *before* `features/entries/` exists. Yet AD-6's example ("`entries/domain` exposes `SaveEntryUseCase`") and the Structural Seed both attribute `features/entries/` and its `SaveEntryUseCase` to **RF06/RF07**. The Capability → Architecture Map makes it worse: RF01's row lists only `AD-1, AD-2, AD-9` as governing ADs — AD-6 (cross-feature port) and AD-11 (entry create/read only) are never cited against RF01 at all.
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/reviews/review-adversarial.md:18:A session building RF01 to the letter has no signal that it must scaffold `features/entries/domain/` first; the obvious, AD-1/AD-2/AD-9-compliant move is to build a `createEntry` call straight inside `features/capture/data` (own repository, own `Entry`-shaped DTO, own hive_ce box) because nothing tells it `features/entries/` is the *owning* feature for an entity capture is only using. Two units later, the RF07 session reads the Structural Seed, sees "`entries/` — RF06, RF07 … exposes `SaveEntryUseCase` (AD-6)," and — also fully AD-compliant — builds its *own* `EntriesRepository`/`Entry` model/hive_ce box from scratch for listing. Both are AD-1/AD-2/AD-6-literal. The result: two `Entry` models, two cache boxes, two repository owners of the same backend resource, and capture's writes never reach whatever cache/sync-badge state (AD-10) RF07 built, because RF07 didn't know capture already wrote one.
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/reviews/review-adversarial.md:65:## 5. RF06 (semantic search) vs `core/cache` (AD-9) — offline fallback semantics for search are undefined, and requirements.md itself is split
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/reviews/review-adversarial.md:67:**Scenario.** AD-9 states a blanket rule: "Read operations transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache." `GET /entries/search` is a read (`entries.search`, `bearerAuth`, `x-cerne-function: entries-search`). But requirements.md is internally inconsistent about what that means for *search* specifically: §6's RF06 AC says "Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection… offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing" (implying a cache-backed, degraded-but-present offline experience), while §13's error-taxonomy table lists `NETWORK_OFFLINE` as "action blocked (see RF04/**RF06**)" (implying search is simply blocked offline, like a write).
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/reviews/review-adversarial.md:69:The spine never resolves this contradiction — AD-9 just repeats the generic "reads fall back to cache" rule without addressing that semantic search has no meaningful local fallback (there's no on-device embedding index; the cache only holds previously-*fetched* entries, not a search index). Two sessions building RF06 independently, both reading AD-9 literally, could land on:
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/reviews/review-adversarial.md:71:- **Session B:** search inherently requires a live embedding call it cannot serve from cache, so it should behave like a write under AD-9 — return `Either.left(NetworkOffline)` immediately, no cache attempt, matching the error-taxonomy table.
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/reviews/review-adversarial.md:73:Both comply with AD-9's text; they produce opposite UX (silently-different "results" vs. an explicit blocked-action error), and whichever a given session picks, nothing in the spine would flag it as wrong — yet RF06's own AC explicitly anticipates this exact ambiguity.
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/reviews/review-adversarial.md:75:**Real or closed?** Real — and already flagged as fuzzy by requirements.md itself, which makes it worse that the spine's AD-9 doesn't resolve it (the Deferred section even calls out the search+filter combination as open, but not this offline-semantics split).
_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/reviews/review-adversarial.md:77:**Proposed fix.** Tighten AD-9: *"AD-9's cache-fallback rule applies only to reads that return previously-synced records as-is (`entries.list`, `entries.get`, `chat.sessions.list`, `chat.messages.list`). 1	import 'package:fpdart/fpdart.dart';
2	
3	import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
4	
5	/// Story 2.4's one DI-singleton access point for the account's
6	/// `biometricEnabled` preference — mirrors `features/vault/domain/
7	/// repositories/vault_repository.dart`'s stream-plus-sync-getter shape
8	/// (AD-14), except the underlying source of truth is server-side (`PATCH
9	/// /account/settings`), not on-device.
10	///
11	/// [currentBiometricEnabled] is the single source both
12	/// `core/navigation/app_router.dart` (feeding `VaultLockScreen`'s
13	/// `attemptBiometricFirst`) and the Configurações toggle read — never a
14	/// second, independently-tracked copy of the same boolean.
15	abstract class AccountSettingsRepository {
16	  /// The exact [Failure.message] [setBiometricEnabled] returns when a call
17	  /// is discarded for being superseded by a newer one (the generation
18	  /// guard, `AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl._generation`) — an internal
19	  /// control-flow signal, not a real error, since the winning call already
20	  /// settled the value correctly by the time this one resolves.
21	  /// `AccountSettingsCubit` recognizes this exact string to suppress it
22	  /// from the UI rather than showing a raw, English, internal message.
23	  static const supersededMessage = 'Superseded by a newer preference update';
24	
25	  /// Broadcast stream of the current `biometricEnabled` preference. Like
26	  /// `VaultRepository.statusStream`, this always has a value from the
27	  /// moment the repository is constructed (`true`) — a late subscriber
28	  /// still immediately replays that cached value.
29	  Stream<bool> get biometricEnabledStream;
30	
31	  /// The last value emitted on [biometricEnabledStream], read
32	  /// synchronously — starts `true` (never `null`) so a cold boot before
33	  /// [fetchBiometricEnabled] resolves still degrades to "try biometric
34	  /// first" (Design Notes), never silent PIN-only.
35	  bool get currentBiometricEnabled;
36	
37	  /// Boot-time read: `PATCH /account/settings` called with `{}` — no GET
38	  /// endpoint exists for this resource (Boundaries). A successful response
39	  /// updates [currentBiometricEnabled]/[biometricEnabledStream] to the
40	  /// server's value; any [Failure] is swallowed (fire-and-forget, like
41	  /// `SessionRepository.restoreSession()`) and leaves
42	  /// [currentBiometricEnabled] exactly as it was.
43	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> fetchBiometricEnabled();
44	
45	  /// Story 2.4's optimistic toggle: [currentBiometricEnabled]/
46	  /// [biometricEnabledStream] flip to [enabled] immediately, before the
47	  /// `PATCH {"biometricEnabled": enabled}` call even starts (RNF01,
48	  /// <100ms) — then, on failure, revert back to the prior value and
49	  /// return `Left` so the caller can surface the `Failure`'s message. A
50	  /// successful PATCH leaves the optimistic value in place and returns
51	  /// `Right(unit)`.
52	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> setBiometricEnabled(bool enabled);
53	
54	  /// Releases the underlying stream resource. Wired as `get_it`'s

## Intent

**Problem:** There is no way to capture a journal Entry yet — `features/entries/` and `features/capture/` are empty scaffolds, the Home/Chat screen has no "+" entry point, and no offline-detection/banner pattern exists anywhere in the app.

**Approach:** Stand up `features/entries/` (Entry entity, `EntriesRepository.create` port, entries Hive box) and `features/capture/` (Insertion Modal bottom sheet with 3 tabs), add a minimal "+" control to the Home/Chat placeholder that opens it, and build the app's first connectivity/offline-banner pattern to gate that control. Only the Texto tab is functional this story.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `features/entries/domain` owns `Entry` (plain class, no freezed — mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`), `EntrySource` enum (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), and `EntriesRepository` (abstract, one method: `create`). `features/capture/` imports only `entries/domain`, never `entries/data` or `entries/presentation` (RNF06).

Close "x" always present. Opens on Texto, all 3 tabs idle/empty.
- Texto tab: text field + Salvar. Salvar fires `POST /entries`; success closes the modal; failure shows `Failure.message` inline and re-enables Salvar (no auto-retry — reuse the existing `Failure.fromCode`/`retryable` mapping as-is).
- "+" control on `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen`: opens the modal; disabled and styled with a new `OfflineBanner`/connectivity pattern (`core/widgets/`, `core/network/connectivity_service.dart`) while offline — this is the app's first instance of that pattern (UX-DR30's "chat send" treatment doesn't exist in code yet to copy from).
- 44pt tap targets, Dynamic Type with no truncation, announced labels for every state change (no color-only signal).

**Ask First:** none identified — docs/input is silent on the exact offline-detection mechanism and the connectivity package choice is this story's own technical decision (AGENTS.md policy).

**Never:**
- Implement Áudio/Foto tab capture logic (render idle/empty only — Stories 3.2/3.3).
- Implement the full cross-tab cancel-safety rule (Story 3.4) — this story only needs the trivial case: the text tab never calls `create` except on explicit Salvar.
- Build the full chat composer (text field + send icon) — RF04's scope. Add only the "+" tap target.
- Add `GET /entries`, listing, search, or any `Entry` fields beyond `{id, content, source, chatMessageId, occurredAt, serverRevision, createdAt, updatedAt}` (tags/piiStatus/embeddingStatus belong to later epics).
- Use the shared `Resource<T>` type for capture's state — capture defines its own sealed state class.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Happy path save | Texto tab, non-empty text, tap Salvar | `POST /entries` (`source: manual`) fires; on success modal closes, returns to Home | N/A |

- [ ] Unit/widget tests under `test/features/entries/`, `test/features/capture/`, `test/core/network/connectivity_service_test.dart` covering the I/O matrix above.

## Design Notes

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- add `durationSheetUp = Duration(milliseconds: 200)` -- no entrance-animation token exists yet (RNF08).
- [ ] `pubspec.yaml` -- add `connectivity_plus` -- enables proactive online/offline signal for the "+" gate.
- [ ] `lib/core/network/connectivity_service.dart` (new) -- `Stream<bool> onlineStream` + `bool get isOnline` wrapping `connectivity_plus` -- the one connectivity source future offline-gated controls (chat send) will reuse.
- [ ] `lib/core/widgets/offline_banner.dart` (new) -- reusable banner using `DesignTokens.colorInfoOffline` -- first instance of UX-DR30's treatment.

- [ ] `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` (new) -- implements `create`; on success writes to the `entries` Hive box keyed by id; maps `EntryDto` → `Entry`.
- [ ] `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart` (new) -- registers datasource/repository, opens/registers the `entries` Hive box.
- [ ] `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` -- wire `Hive.initFlutter()` + `registerEntriesFeature()` + `registerCaptureFeature()`.
- [ ] `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit.dart` (new) -- own sealed state (active tab, text, saving/error); calls `EntriesRepository.create` directly on Salvar.
- [ ] `lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart` (new) -- 3-tab bottom sheet; Texto functional, Áudio/Foto idle placeholders.
- [ ] `lib/features/capture/capture_injection.dart` (new) -- registers `TextEntryCubit`.

## Design Notes

- **Connectivity package:** `connectivity_plus` is the chosen mechanism (docs/input is silent; AGENTS.md policy says decide and proceed) — a thin `ConnectivityService` wraps it so no other file depends on the package directly, keeping future swaps cheap.
- **Hive storage shape:** entries are cached as raw `Map<String, dynamic>` (via `EntryDto.toJson()`), not a generated `HiveObject`/`TypeAdapter` — avoids adapter codegen for a box nothing reads yet (reads start in Epic 4); revisit if a future story needs typed queries.

---
title: 'Story 3.1: Text Entry Capture & Insertion Modal Shell'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-04'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** There is no way to capture a journal Entry yet — `features/entries/` and `features/capture/` are empty scaffolds, and the Home/Chat screen has no "+" entry point.

**Approach:** Stand up `features/entries/` (Entry entity, `EntriesRepository.create` port, entries Hive box) and `features/capture/` (Insertion Modal bottom sheet with 3 tabs), and add a minimal "+" control to the Home/Chat placeholder that opens it. Only the Texto tab is functional this story.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `features/entries/domain` owns `Entry` (plain class, no freezed — mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`), `EntrySource` enum (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), and `EntriesRepository` (abstract, one method: `create`). `features/capture/` imports only `entries/domain`, never `entries/data` or `entries/presentation` (RNF06).
- `EntriesRepository.create` → `Either<Failure, Entry>`, posts to `entries-create` via the shared `ApiClient.post`, source=`manual` for this story. On success, write the entry through to the `entries` Hive box (`Box<Map>`, keyed by id) — first use of `hive_ce` in the app.
- Insertion Modal: `showModalBottomSheet(isScrollControlled: true, barrierColor: DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy)`, `radiusLg` top corners, `elevation2`, new `DesignTokens.durationSheetUp` (200ms) entrance, skipped under Reduce Motion. 3 equal-width tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto); only the active tab fills `colorPrimary`. Close "x" always present. Opens on Texto, all 3 tabs idle/empty.
- Texto tab: text field + Salvar. Salvar fires `POST /entries`; success closes the modal; failure (including offline, via the existing `Failure.networkOffline`) shows `Failure.message` inline and re-enables Salvar — no auto-retry, reuse `Failure.fromCode`/`retryable` as-is.
- "+" control on `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen`: always tappable, opens the modal. No proactive offline detection or banner in this story (deferred — see Spec Change Log / `deferred-work.md`); an offline save attempt surfaces the same way any other failed save does.
- 44pt tap targets, Dynamic Type with no truncation, announced labels for every state change (no color-only signal).

**Ask First:** none identified.

**Never:**
- Implement Áudio/Foto tab capture logic (render idle/empty only — Stories 3.2/3.3).
- Implement the full cross-tab cancel-safety rule (Story 3.4) — this story only needs the trivial case: the text tab never calls `create` except on explicit Salvar.
- Build the full chat composer (text field + send icon) — RF04's scope. Add only the "+" tap target.
- Add a connectivity service, offline banner, or any proactive offline-disabling of "+" — deferred (see `deferred-work.md`); no existing pattern to reuse, and the prototype doesn't represent this state.
- Add `GET /entries`, listing, search, or any `Entry` fields beyond `{id, content, source, chatMessageId, occurredAt, serverRevision, createdAt, updatedAt}` (tags/piiStatus/embeddingStatus belong to later epics).
- Use the shared `Resource<T>` type for capture's state — capture defines its own sealed state class.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Happy path save | Texto tab, non-empty text, tap Salvar | `POST /entries` (`source: manual`) fires; on success modal closes, returns to Home | N/A |
| Modal open resets | "+" tapped | Opens on Texto; all 3 tabs idle/empty regardless of prior session | N/A |
| Save fails (incl. offline) | Salvar tapped, backend call returns a mapped error code (e.g. `NETWORK_OFFLINE`) | Inline message from `Failure.message`; Salvar re-enabled; modal stays open | `Failure.fromCode`, no auto-retry |
| Cancel before save | "x" tapped or user leaves with unsaved text | Modal closes/resets; no `POST /entries` fires | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

**Problem:** There is no way to capture a journal Entry yet — `features/entries/` and `features/capture/` are empty scaffolds, and the Home/Chat screen has no "+" entry point.

**Approach:** Stand up `features/entries/` (Entry entity, `EntriesRepository.create` port, entries Hive box) and `features/capture/` (Insertion Modal bottom sheet with 3 tabs), and add a minimal "+" control to the Home/Chat placeholder that opens it. Only the Texto tab is functional this story.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `features/entries/domain` owns `Entry` (plain class, no freezed — mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`), `EntrySource` enum (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), and `EntriesRepository` (abstract, one method: `create`). `features/capture/` imports only `entries/domain`, never `entries/data` or `entries/presentation` (RNF06).
- `EntriesRepository.create` → `Either<Failure, Entry>`, posts to `entries-create` via the shared `ApiClient.post`, source=`manual` for this story. On success, write the entry through to the `entries` Hive box (`Box<Map>`, keyed by id) — first use of `hive_ce` in the app.
- Insertion Modal: `showModalBottomSheet(isScrollControlled: true, barrierColor: DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy)`, `radiusLg` top corners, `elevation2`, new `DesignTokens.durationSheetUp` (200ms) entrance, skipped under Reduce Motion. 3 equal-width tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto); only the active tab fills `colorPrimary`. Close "x" always present. Opens on Texto, all 3 tabs idle/empty.
- Texto tab: text field + Salvar. Salvar fires `POST /entries`; success closes the modal; failure (including offline, via the existing `Failure.networkOffline`) shows `Failure.message` inline and re-enables Salvar — no auto-retry, reuse `Failure.fromCode`/`retryable` as-is.
- "+" control on `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen`: always tappable, opens the modal. No proactive offline detection or banner in this story (deferred — see Spec Change Log / `deferred-work.md`); an offline save attempt surfaces the same way any other failed save does.
- 44pt tap targets, Dynamic Type with no truncation, announced labels for every state change (no color-only signal).

**Ask First:** none identified.

**Never:**
- Implement Áudio/Foto tab capture logic (render idle/empty only — Stories 3.2/3.3).
- Implement the full cross-tab cancel-safety rule (Story 3.4) — this story only needs the trivial case: the text tab never calls `create` except on explicit Salvar.
- Build the full chat composer (text field + send icon) — RF04's scope. Add only the "+" tap target.
- Add a connectivity service, offline banner, or any proactive offline-disabling of "+" — deferred (see `deferred-work.md`); no existing pattern to reuse, and the prototype doesn't represent this state.
- Add `GET /entries`, listing, search, or any `Entry` fields beyond `{id, content, source, chatMessageId, occurredAt, serverRevision, createdAt, updatedAt}` (tags/piiStatus/embeddingStatus belong to later epics).
- Use the shared `Resource<T>` type for capture's state — capture defines its own sealed state class.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Happy path save | Texto tab, non-empty text, tap Salvar | `POST /entries` (`source: manual`) fires; on success modal closes, returns to Home | N/A |
| Modal open resets | "+" tapped | Opens on Texto; all 3 tabs idle/empty regardless of prior session | N/A |
| Save fails (incl. offline) | Salvar tapped, backend call returns a mapped error code (e.g. `NETWORK_OFFLINE`) | Inline message from `Failure.message`; Salvar re-enabled; modal stays open | `Failure.fromCode`, no auto-retry |
| Cancel before save | "x" tapped or user leaves with unsaved text | Modal closes/resets; no `POST /entries` fires | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart:76-130` (`HomeChatPlaceholderScreen`) — add the "+" entry point here; body is currently a pure placeholder (RF04 not built), no composer exists.
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart:85` (`colorScrimHeavy`, already reserved for "a later story's insertion modal"), `:199` (`radiusLg`), `:218` (`elevation2`) — reuse as-is; add `durationSheetUp` near these, no `Duration`/motion token exists yet.
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:67-83` (`Failure.fromCode`) — reuse unchanged; already generic, no new mapping needed.
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:52-62` (`post`) — call via the new `EntriesRemoteDataSource`.
- `lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart:20-24` (`anonKeyOnlyFunctions`) — `entries-create` is not in that set, so it auto-gets the user bearer token; no changes needed.
- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:26-84` (`setupCoreDependencies`) — add `Hive.initFlutter()` + `registerEntriesFeature()` + `registerCaptureFeature()`, after the existing `registerAccountFeature()` call.
- `lib/features/account/account_injection.dart`, `account_remote_data_source.dart`, `account_settings_dto.dart`, `account_settings_repository_impl.dart`, `account_settings_cubit.dart` — structural patterns to mirror (DI registration, `ApiClient` datasource, `@JsonSerializable` DTO, repository impl, cubit calling repository directly — no use-case layer exists in this codebase).
- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/authenticated_user.dart` — plain-class entity pattern (no freezed) to mirror for `Entry`.
- `lib/features/entries/{data,domain,presentation}/.gitkeep`, `lib/features/capture/{data,domain,presentation}/.gitkeep` — empty scaffolds to fill.
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:327-449` — `entries-create` request/response schema.
- `pubspec.yaml:42-43` — `hive_ce`/`hive_ce_flutter` already a dependency, unused until now.
- `test/features/account/**` — test directory layout to mirror under `test/features/entries/` and `test/features/capture/`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- add `durationSheetUp = Duration(milliseconds: 200)` -- no entrance-animation token exists yet (RNF08).
- [ ] `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart` (new) -- `Entry` class + `EntrySource` enum -- mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`.
- [ ] `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` (new) -- abstract `EntriesRepository.create(...)` → `Future<Either<Failure, Entry>>` -- the port later epics extend.
- [ ] `lib/features/entries/data/models/entry_dto.dart` (+ generated `.g.dart`) -- `@JsonSerializable()` mirroring the response `data` object.
- [ ] `lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` (new) -- posts to `entries-create` via `ApiClient.post`, decodes `EntryDto`.
- [ ] `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` (new) -- implements `create`; on success writes to the `entries` Hive box keyed by id; maps `EntryDto` → `Entry`.
- [ ] `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart` (new) -- registers datasource/repository, opens/registers the `entries` Hive box.
- [ ] `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` -- wire `Hive.initFlutter()` + `registerEntriesFeature()` + `registerCaptureFeature()`.
- [ ] `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit.dart` (new) -- own sealed state (active tab, text, saving/error); calls `EntriesRepository.create` directly on Salvar.
- [ ] `lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart` (new) -- 3-tab bottom sheet; Texto functional, Áudio/Foto idle placeholders.
- [ ] `lib/features/capture/capture_injection.dart` (new) -- registers `TextEntryCubit`.
- [ ] `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` -- add the always-tappable "+" control to `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` that opens `InsertionModal`.
- [ ] Unit/widget tests under `test/features/entries/`, `test/features/capture/` covering the I/O matrix above.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given `features/entries/` doesn't exist yet, when this story is built, then `entries/domain` owns `Entry` + `EntriesRepository(create)` + the entries Hive box, and `features/capture/` never imports `entries/data` or `entries/presentation`.
- Given the "+" control, when tapped, then the Insertion Modal opens with the `sheetUp` entrance (skipped under Reduce Motion).
- Given any state change this story introduces, when a screen reader is active, then an announced label accompanies it — never color/animation alone.
- Given `fvm flutter analyze` and `fvm flutter test`, then both report zero issues / all green.

## Spec Change Log

- 2026-11-04 — Token-count checkpoint (step-02): spec exceeded 1600 tokens (~2676) because it bundled a proactive offline-detection/banner pattern that doesn't exist anywhere in the app yet. Human chose [S] Split: carved the connectivity/banner work out to `deferred-work.md` and narrowed this story's "+" control to always-tappable, with offline failures surfacing through the existing reactive `Failure.networkOffline` path. KEEP: the `entries`/`capture` feature stand-up, Hive write-through, and modal-shell scope are otherwise unchanged from the original investigation.

## Design Notes

- **Hive storage shape:** entries are cached as raw `Map<String, dynamic>` (via `EntryDto.toJson()`), not a generated `HiveObject`/`TypeAdapter` — avoids adapter codegen for a box nothing reads yet (reads start in Epic 4); revisit if a future story needs typed queries.
- **No use-case layer:** `TextEntryCubit` calls `EntriesRepository.create` directly, matching this codebase's existing convention (`AccountSettingsCubit`, `AuthCubit`) — RF10's reuse requirement is satisfied by the port itself, not an extra use-case class.
- **"+" is minimal:** a single tappable control, not the RF04 composer bar — avoids building chat-input UI that RF04 will define and may not match.

Shared sub-step for updating `sprint-status.yaml` during build. Called from any route (plan-code-review, one-shot, future routes) with a `target_status` parameter.

## Preconditions

Skip this entire file (return to caller) if ANY of:
- `story_key` is unset
- `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` does not exist on disk

1. Load the FULL `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` file.
2. Find the `development_status` entry matching `{story_key}`. If not found, warn the user once (`"{story_key} not found in sprint-status; skipping sprint sync"`) and return to caller.

4. Set `development_status[{story_key}]` to `{target_status}`.

6. Refresh `last_updated` to the current date.
7. Save the file, preserving ALL comments and structure including STATUS DEFINITIONS and WORKFLOW NOTES.

  - `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart` — `Entry` plain class + `EntrySource` enum, mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`.
  - `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` — abstract `EntriesRepository.create({content, source}) -> Either<Failure, Entry>`.
  - `lib/features/entries/data/models/entry_dto.dart` (+ generated `entry_dto.g.dart`) — `@JsonSerializable()` DTO; `EntrySource` round-trips via its own `.name`.
  - `lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` — posts `{content, source}` to `entries-create` via `ApiClient.post`.

  - `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit.dart` — `CaptureTab` enum + a hand-written sealed `TextEntryState` (Idle/Saving/Saved/Error, never the shared `Resource<T>`), `TextEntryCubit` calling `EntriesRepository.create` directly (no use-case layer, per Design Notes).

Texto tab is fully functional; Áudio/Foto render idle placeholders only.

  **Wiring**:
  - `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` — added `durationSheetUp = Duration(milliseconds: 200)`.
  - `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` — added `Hive.initFlutter()` + `registerEntriesFeature()` + `registerCaptureFeature()` after `registerAccountFeature()`.

  Supplying a custom `transitionAnimationController` to `showModalBottomSheet` means **you** own disposal — but `showModalBottomSheet`'s returned `Future` resolves as soon as `Navigator.pop()` is called, *before* the framework's own `reverse()` exit animation on that same controller finishes.   - `test/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl_test.dart` (Hive write success/failure, mocked `Box<Map>`)
  - `test/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit_test.dart`
  - `test/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal_test.dart` (full I/O matrix against the real widget: happy path, offline/failure, cancel-via-"x", Reduce Motion)
  - `test/core/navigation/placeholder_screens_test.dart` — new case for the "+" control
  - `test/core/di/bootstrap_integration_test.dart` and `test/main_test.dart` extended to cover the new DI chain
  
  **Infra note**: `setupCoreDependencies()` now calls `Hive.initFlutter()`, which transitively needs `path_provider`. Added `test/support/fake_path_provider_platform.dart` (a `PathProviderPlatform` override returning a temp dir) and wired it into both `bootstrap_integration_test.dart` and `main_test.dart`, plus `Hive.close()` in their `tearDown` (otherwise a box opened in one test leaks into the next, since Hive silently returns an already-open box rather than reopening at a new path). Added `path_provider_platform_interface` as a dev dependency for this.
  
  ## Verification
  
  - `fvm flutter pub get` — resolved, no conflicts.
  - `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` — generated `entry_dto.g.dart` cleanly.
  - `fvm flutter analyze` — zero issues.
  - `fvm flutter test` — **394 tests, all passing** (full suite, including the pre-existing suites I touched for DI/Hive wiring).
  
  ## Boundaries honored (double-checked)
  
  - `grep` confirms `features/capture/` never imports `entries/data` or `entries/presentation`.
  - `entries/domain` imports neither `flutter` nor `data/`.
  - No Áudio/Foto capture logic — idle placeholders only.
  - No `GET /entries`, no extra `Entry` fields beyond the 8 named.
  - "+" is a bare FAB, not the RF04 composer.
  - No connectivity service/offline banner was added.
  
  ## Risks / things worth a second look
  
  - The FAB on `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` is my own visual choice (spec didn't specify the exact widget) — a `FloatingActionButton` with `colorAccent`/`colorOnAccent`, sized well above the 44pt floor. If the prototype or a later story expects a different placement/shape, this is the one spot to revisit.
  - `EntriesRepository.create` takes only `{content, source}` — I deliberately left `chatMessageId`/`occurredAt`/`mediaDurationSeconds` out of the port signature since this story never needs them; Stories 3.2/3.3/RF10 will need to decide whether to extend this method's signature or add overloads.
  - `occurredAt`/`createdAt`/`updatedAt` are kept as raw ISO-8601 strings (not parsed to `DateTime`) on both the DTO and the domain `Entry` — a deliberate, documented simplicity choice since nothing reads them yet.
  
</agent-message>

# Verification Gap Review

**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.

The main verification gap shapes are:

1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.

## Evidence Rules

- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.

## Review Sequence

### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change

Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.

Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.

Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.

If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).

### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed

Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.

Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.

### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used

Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.

Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.

### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test

For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. If no such regression exists, drop the path; untested downstream code is not a finding.

A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.

Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.

- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.

A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.

For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.

Common patterns:

- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.

### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real

Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.

Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.

Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.

Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.

## OUTPUT FORMAT

Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.

```markdown
### <one-line title naming the gap>

- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
- **Existing test evidence:**
  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
- **Demonstration:**
  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
```

If you noticed genuine non-gap problems while tracing verification, append:

```markdown
## Other findings

- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
```

When you find no verification gaps and no other findings, output exactly this single line, not an empty response:

`No verification gaps found.`

## CONTENT SOURCE

Review the content supplied under "Review content:" in the message that launched you. If none is supplied, stop with exactly: `No verification gaps found.`

31	+## Intent
32	+
33	+**Problem:** There is no way to capture a journal Entry yet — `features/entries/` and `features/capture/` are empty scaffolds, and the Home/Chat screen has no "+" entry point.
34	+
35	+**Approach:** Stand up `features/entries/` (Entry entity, `EntriesRepository.create` port, entries Hive box) and `features/capture/` (Insertion Modal bottom sheet with 3 tabs), and add a minimal "+" control to the Home/Chat placeholder that opens it. Only the Texto tab is functional this story.
36	+
37	+## Boundaries & Constraints
38	+
39	+**Always:**
40	+- `features/entries/domain` owns `Entry` (plain class, no freezed — mirrors `AuthenticatedUser`), `EntrySource` enum (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), and `EntriesRepository` (abstract, one method: `create`). `features/capture/` imports only `entries/domain`, never `entries/data` or `entries/presentation` (RNF06).
41	+- `EntriesRepository.create` → `Either<Failure, Entry>`, posts to `entries-create` via the shared `ApiClient.post`, source=`manual` for this story. On success, write the entry through to the `entries` Hive box (`Box<Map>`, keyed by id) — first use of `hive_ce` in the app.
42	+- Insertion Modal: `showModalBottomSheet(isScrollControlled: true, barrierColor: DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy)`, `radiusLg` top corners, `elevation2`, new `DesignTokens.durationSheetUp` (200ms) entrance, skipped under Reduce Motion. 3 equal-width tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto); only the active tab fills `colorPrimary`. Close "x" always present. Opens on Texto, all 3 tabs idle/empty.
43	+- Texto tab: text field + Salvar. Salvar fires `POST /entries`; success closes the modal; failure (including offline, via the existing `Failure.networkOffline`) shows `Failure.message` inline and re-enables Salvar — no auto-retry, reuse `Failure.fromCode`/`retryable` as-is.
44	+- "+" control on `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen`: always tappable, opens the modal. No proactive offline detection or banner in this story (deferred — see Spec Change Log / `deferred-work.md`); an offline save attempt surfaces the same way any other failed save does.
45	+- 44pt tap targets, Dynamic Type with no truncation, announced labels for every state change (no color-only signal).
46	+

268	+/// Áudio/Foto)". Only [texto] is functional this story; [audio]/[foto]
269	+/// render idle, non-interactive placeholders (Stories 3.2/3.3).
270	+enum CaptureTab { texto, audio, foto }
271	+
272	+/// Capture's own state for the Insertion Modal — never the shared
273	+/// `Resource<T>` (Boundaries). A sealed class, not `freezed` (no codegen
274	+/// for this story beyond `entry_dto.g.dart`, Verification): every
275	+/// variant always carries the common [activeTab]/[text] so switching tabs
276	+/// or typing never needs to know which variant it's coming from.
277	+sealed class TextEntryState {
278	+  const TextEntryState({required this.activeTab, required this.text});
279	+
280	+  final CaptureTab activeTab;
281	+  final String text;
282	+}
283	+
284	+/// Ready to type/save — the state immediately after the modal opens
285	+/// (Boundaries: "Opens on Texto, all 3 tabs idle/empty"), after a tab
286	+/// switch, and after a keystroke.
287	+class TextEntryIdle extends TextEntryState {
288	+  const TextEntryIdle({required super.activeTab, required super.text});
289	+}
290	+
291	+/// Salvar tapped, `POST /entries` in flight — the I/O matrix's "no
292	+/// auto-retry, no double-submit": `InsertionModal` disables Salvar/the
293	+/// text field for the duration of this state.
294	+class TextEntrySaving extends TextEntryState {
295	+  const TextEntrySaving({required super.activeTab, required super.text});
296	+}
297	+
298	+/// The save attempt succeeded — `InsertionModal`'s listener reacts to
299	+/// this by popping the sheet (I/O matrix: "success closes the modal").
300	+/// Terminal: nothing meaningful follows it for this cubit instance, since
301	+/// the modal (and the factory-scoped cubit backing it) is already
302	+/// closing.
303	+class TextEntrySaved extends TextEntryState {
304	+  const TextEntrySaved({required super.activeTab, required super.text});
305	+}
306	+
307	+/// The last save attempt failed (incl. offline, via the existing
308	+/// `Failure.networkOffline`) — [message] is `Failure.message` verbatim
309	+/// (I/O matrix: "Inline message from `Failure.message`"); Salvar is
310	+/// re-enabled, the modal stays open, no auto-retry.
311	+class TextEntryError extends TextEntryState {
312	+  const TextEntryError({
313	+    required super.activeTab,
314	+    required super.text,
315	+    required this.message,
316	+  });
317	+
318	+  final String message;
319	+}
320	+
321	+/// Drives `InsertionModal`. Calls [EntriesRepository.create] directly on
322	+/// [save] — no use-case layer, matching this codebase's existing
323	+/// convention (Design Notes: `AccountSettingsCubit`/`AuthCubit`). A fresh,
324	+/// `get_it`-factory-scoped instance per "+" tap (Boundaries: "Modal open
325	+/// resets") — starting state is always [TextEntryIdle] on
326	+/// [CaptureTab.texto] with empty text, so no explicit reset method is
327	+/// needed the way `AccountSettingsCubit.clearStaleError()` needs one for
328	+/// its own long-lived singleton.
329	+class TextEntryCubit extends Cubit<TextEntryState> {
330	+  TextEntryCubit(this._repository)
331	+    : super(const TextEntryIdle(activeTab: CaptureTab.texto, text: ''));
332	+
333	+  final EntriesRepository _repository;
334	+
335	+  /// Switches the active tab, preserving whatever Texto text was already
336	+  /// typed (Never: the full cross-tab cancel-safety rule is Story 3.4's

338	+  /// switch without losing in-progress text or firing any `create` call).
339	+  /// Dropped while [TextEntrySaving]/[TextEntryError] is only cosmetic —
340	+  /// a save already in flight for the Texto tab is untouched by this,

342	+  void selectTab(CaptureTab tab) {
343	+    if (tab == state.activeTab) {
344	+      return;
345	+    }
346	+    emit(TextEntryIdle(activeTab: tab, text: state.text));
347	+  }
348	+
349	+  /// Mirrors the Texto field's own `TextEditingController` into this
350	+  /// cubit's state, so [save] has the latest typed text to send. Ignored
351	+  /// while a save is already in flight — the field is disabled in that
352	+  /// state (`InsertionModal`), so this should never fire then regardless.
353	+  void updateText(String text) {
354	+    if (state is TextEntrySaving) {
355	+      return;
356	+    }
357	+    emit(TextEntryIdle(activeTab: state.activeTab, text: text));
358	+  }

360	+  /// I/O matrix's "Happy path save"/"Save fails" rows: fires `POST
361	+  /// /entries` with `source: manual` (Boundaries — the only source this
362	+  /// story ever sends) for whatever non-empty text is currently typed. A
363	+  /// blank/whitespace-only text never calls [EntriesRepository.create] —
364	+  /// `InsertionModal` already disables Salvar for that case, but this is
365	+  /// the authoritative guard regardless of how `save()` is invoked.
366	+  Future<void> save() async {
367	+    final text = state.text.trim();
368	+    if (text.isEmpty || state is TextEntrySaving) {
369	+      return;
370	+    }
371	+    final activeTab = state.activeTab;
372	+    emit(TextEntrySaving(activeTab: activeTab, text: text));
373	+    final result = await _repository.create(

381	+    if (isClosed) {
382	+      return;
383	+    }
384	+    result.match(
